'''John Allen King''' (15 April 1938 – 30 March 2016) was an English [[association football|football]] player and [[Manager (association football)|manager]].<ref name="death">{{cite web|title=Johnny King 1938-2016|url=http://www.tranmererovers.co.uk/news/article/johnny-king-1938-2016-3033736.aspx|work=Mark Palios, Chairman of Tranmere Rovers FC|access-date=31 March 2016}}</ref> He is widely regarded as being the most successful manager in the history of [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] and had a stand at [[Prenton Park]] named in his honour in 2002. In November 2014, a statue of King was unveiled outside the ground.

He played at [[wing half]] and made 411 league appearances in a 14-year career in the [[English Football League|Football League]]. He began his career at [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], playing for the club in the top flight between 1957 and 1960. He then moved on to Tranmere Rovers via [[Bournemouth & Boscombe Athletic F.C.|Bournemouth & Boscombe Athletic]]. He helped Rovers to win [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] out of the [[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]] in 1966–67, before he signed with [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] in June 1968. He helped the "Valiants" to promotion out of the Fourth Division in 1969–70 before he joined [[Non-League football|non-League]] [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] in May 1971.

He found more success as a manager than a player, gaining his first management post at former club Tranmere Rovers in April 1975. He guided Tranmere to promotion out of the Fourth Division in 1975–76 before he was dismissed in September 1980. He then had successful spells in charge at non-League clubs [[Northwich Victoria F.C.|Northwich Victoria]] (winning the [[FA Trophy]] in [[1984 FA Trophy final|1984]]) and [[Caernarfon Town F.C.|Caernarfon Town]], before making his return to Tranmere Rovers in 1987. He immediately steered the club away from losing their Football League status before taking them to promotion in 1988–89. He further took them to the [[EFL Trophy|Associate Members' Cup]] title in [[1990 Associate Members' Cup final|1990]], the Football League Trophy final in [[1991 Associate Members' Cup final|1991]], as well as promotion out of the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]] as winners of [[1991 Football League Third Division play-off final|the play-off]]s. His team narrowly missed out on promotion to the [[Premier League]], reaching the [[English Football League play-offs|play-offs]] three times between 1993 and 1995, also reaching the semi-finals of the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]]. He became Tranmere's [[Director of football]] in April 1996.

==Early life==

According to [[British Library]] records, John King was born in the [[Marylebone]] district of London on 15 April 1938. His parents, Henry J. King and Maud H. Dryland, were married in Ashford in Kent in 1934.

==Playing career==
King started his career at [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in 1957. He made 48 [[Football League First Division|First Division]] appearances at [[Goodison Park]] under [[Ian Buchan]] and [[Johnny Carey]] over the course of the [[1957–58 Football League|1957–58]], [[1958–59 Football League|1958–59]], and [[1959–60 Football League|1959–60]] campaigns. He then moved on to [[Bournemouth & Boscombe Athletic F.C.|Bournemouth & Boscombe Athletic]], playing 21 [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]] games under [[Don Welsh]], before he joined [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] and being signed by [[Walter Galbraith]].<ref name="death"/> Rovers were [[Promotion and relegation|relegated]] out of the Third Division in [[1960–61 Football League|1960–61]]. New [[Manager (association football)|manager]] [[Dave Russell (footballer)|Dave Russell]] led them to a 15th-place finish in the [[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]] in [[1961–62 Football League|1961–62]]. They then reached eighth in [[1962–63 Football League|1962–63]] and seventh in [[1963–64 Football League|1963–64]], before finishing fifth in [[1964–65 Football League|1964–65]], just one place and one point behind [[Promotion and relegation|promoted]] [[Oxford United F.C.|Oxford United]]. They came even closer in [[1965–66 Football League|1965–66]], finishing behind promoted [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]] on goal average. Rovers finally achieved their goal in [[1966–67 Football League|1966–67]], winning promotion in fourth place; they finished four points ahead of fifth-place [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]]. They retained their third-tier status in [[1967–68 Football League|1967–68]], finishing two places above the relegation zone. Over eight years at [[Prenton Park]], King made 264 appearances in all competitions.

He signed with [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] in June 1968.<ref name="Kent">{{cite book|last=Kent|first=Jeff|title=Port Vale Personalities|publisher=Witan Books|page=163|year=1996|isbn=0-9529152-0-0}}</ref> He made 46 appearances in [[1968–69 Port Vale F.C. season|1968–69]], helping [[Gordon Lee (footballer)|Gordon Lee]]'s "Valiants" to a 13th-place finish in the Fourth Division.<ref name="Kent"/> He played alongside [[Roy Sproson]] in a team which was based around defence. He played in a goalless home draw with [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea Town]] on 18 October 1969, despite having [[chickenpox]] at the time, and played a total of 41 games in the [[1969–70 Port Vale F.C. season|1969–70]] promotion season.<ref name="Kent"/> King chipped his ankle bone in November 1970 and was sidelined for four months; therefore, he could only play 27 games in [[1970–71 Port Vale F.C. season|1970–71]].<ref name="Kent"/> He left on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]] to [[Northern Premier League]] side [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] in May 1971,<ref name="Kent"/> making 12 appearances in the [[1971–72 Northern Premier League|1971–72]] campaign, his only season at [[Springfield Park (Wigan)|Springfield Park]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Hayes|first=Dean|title=The Latics: The Official History of Wigan Athletic F.C.|year=1996|publisher=Yore Publications|location=Harefield|isbn=1-874427-91-7}}</ref>

==Managerial career==

===Tranmere Rovers===
King was first appointed as [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]] manager in April 1975 and led his charges to promotion out of the [[Football League Fourth Division|Fourth Division]] in [[1975–76 Tranmere Rovers F.C. season|1975–76]]. He stabilised the club in the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]] in [[1976–77 Football League|1976–77]], and another mid-table finish followed in [[1977–78 Football League|1977–78]]. However, Rovers were relegated in 23rd place in [[1978–79 Football League|1978–79]], finishing 12 points behind 20th place [[Chesterfield F.C.|Chesterfield]]. Rovers then dropped to 15th in the bottom tier in [[1979–80 Football League|1979–80]]. King was dismissed in September 1980,<ref name = "stand"/> but new manager, [[Bryan Hamilton]], could not prevent Tranmere from finishing in the re-election zone in [[1980–81 Football League|1980–81]].

===Northwich Victoria===
King moved on to [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] as a [[Coach (sport)|coach]] before taking the reins at [[Northwich Victoria F.C.|Northwich Victoria]] in October 1981. He took the club to sixth in the [[National League (division)|Alliance Premier League]] in [[1981–82 Alliance Premier League|1981–82]], eighth in [[1982–83 Alliance Premier League|1982–83]], and seventh in [[1983–84 Alliance Premier League|1983–84]]. He took Victoria to [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley]] in [[1983 FA Trophy final|1983]], where they lost 2–0 to [[Telford United F.C.|Telford United]] in the [[FA Trophy]]. They travelled to Wembley again for the FA Trophy final in [[1984 FA Trophy final|1984]], though a 1–1 draw meant that a [[Replay (sports)|replay]] was held at the [[Victoria Ground]] in [[Stoke-on-Trent]]; Northwich then beat [[Bangor City F.C.|Bangor City]] 2–1 to take the trophy back to [[Drill Field]]. He also led the club to the [[Cheshire Senior Cup]] title in 1984.{{citation needed|date=June 2026}}

===Caernarfon Town===
King took charge at Welsh club [[Caernarfon Town F.C.|Caernarfon Town]].<ref name="Kent" /> At [[Northern Premier League]] side Caernarfon he was at the helm for some of the most successful seasons in the club's history, including the club's 1986–87 [[FA Cup]] run to the third round, recording victories over Football League sides [[Stockport County F.C.|Stockport County]] and [[York City F.C.|York City]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.caernarfononline.co.uk/cofis/hall.html |title=Hall of fame |publisher=Caernarfon Online |access-date=4 September 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725033947/http://www.caernarfononline.co.uk/cofis/hall.html |archive-date=25 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Return to Tranmere Rovers===
King was appointed manager of Tranmere for a second time by [[Peter Johnson (businessman)|Peter Johnson]] towards the end of the [[1986–87 Football League|1986–87]] season, with the club fighting to avoid relegation out of the [[English Football League|Football League]]. Safety was only guaranteed in the last game of the season with a 1–0 home win over [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]]. King signed [[Jim Steel (footballer)|Jim Steel]] to act as a target man for striker [[Ian Muir (English footballer)|Ian Muir]]. The move was inspired, and the team enjoyed considerable success in the following seasons. They rose to a mid-table finish in [[1987–88 Football League|1987–88]], before winning promotion as Fourth Division runners-up in [[1988–89 Tranmere Rovers F.C. season|1988–89]]. Tranmere then finished fourth in the [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]] in [[1989–90 Tranmere Rovers F.C. season|1989–90]], missing out on a second successive promotion after losing 2–0 to [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]] in the [[1990 Football League Third Division play-off final|play-off final]]. They played at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley]] four times in two years, winning the [[EFL Trophy|Associate Members' Cup]] in [[1990 Associate Members' Cup final|1990]] with a 2–1 victory over [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]].<ref name="Daily Post">{{cite news|last1=Welton|first1=Blake|title=Former Caernarfon Town manager and Tranmere Rovers legend John King dies|url=http://www.dailypost.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/former-caernarfon-town-manager-tranmere-11117363|access-date=31 March 2016|work=Daily Post|date=31 March 2016}}</ref> He led the "Superwhites" promotion with a 1–0 win over [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] in the [[1991 Football League Third Division play-off final|1991 play-off final]], after Tranmere finished fifth in [[1990–91 Tranmere Rovers F.C. season|1990–91]]. They also reached the Associate Members' Cup [[1991 Associate Members' Cup final|final]] for a second successive year, losing 3–2 to [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]].

They finished a comfortable 14th in [[1991–92 Football League|1991–92]], before hitting fourth in [[1992–93 Football League|1992–93]]. This qualified them for the [[English Football League play-offs|play-offs]]; however, they were beaten 5–4 on [[aggregate score|aggregate]] by [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]] at the semi-final stage. The club again narrowly missed out on promotion to the [[Premier League]] in [[1993–94 Tranmere Rovers F.C. season|1993–94]], losing to [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] in the play-off semi-finals.<ref name = "Moore">{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-commentary-tranmere-ride-a-new-mersey-beat-1442139.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220613/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-commentary-tranmere-ride-a-new-mersey-beat-1442139.html |archive-date=13 June 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Football Commentary: Tranmere ride a new Mersey beat |last=Moore|first=Glenn|date=10 October 1994|work=The Independent|access-date=25 May 2009}}</ref> They also reached the semi-finals of the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]], losing to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on penalties.

King brought big-name signings such as [[John Aldridge]], [[Pat Nevin]] and [[Gary Stevens (footballer, born 1963)|Gary Stevens]] to [[Prenton Park]], but their crowds did not increase much. The club had to sell players such as [[Steve Vickers (footballer)|Steve Vickers]] and [[Ian Nolan]] to survive.<ref name = "Moore"/> Tranmere nevertheless qualified for the play-offs for a third successive season in [[1994–95 Football League|1994–95]], finishing fifth, before being beaten 3–1 by [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] at the play-off semi-final stage. In April 1996, with Rovers struggling for form in the league, chairman Frank Corfe appointed [[John Aldridge]] as [[player-manager]], and King became [[Director of football]]. They finished the [[1995–96 Football League|1995–96]] campaign in 13th position.

===Recognition by Tranmere Rovers===
The former Borough Road stand at Tranmere Rovers' ground, Prenton Park, was renamed the Johnny King Stand in 2002.<ref name = "stand">{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/t/tranmere_rovers/2016859.stm|title=Tranmere to honour King|date=30 May 2002|work=BBC Sport|access-date=25 May 2009}}</ref> On 1 November 2014, a bronze statue of King, designed by artist Tom Murphy, was unveiled outside the ground   by King himself before the club's home match against [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]]. Ben Harrison of the Tranmere Rovers Supporters Club said that "Johnny King is the club's greatest ever manager and is rightly revered by every Tranmere supporter. A loyal servant as both player and manager, the unparalleled success and style of football played by his teams as we rose from near oblivion to the verge of the Premier League will always be fondly remembered at Prenton Park."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-merseyside-29863239|title=Johnny King: Statue unveiled for Tranmere manager|date=1 November 2014|work=BBC News}}</ref>
